subtitle: How Silver Bore the Fall of the Kshaharatas

panels.shot: dramatic close-up of a silver coin on an anvil, a hammer frozen mid-strike as a new legend descends on an old king's face
panels.action: Nahapana stands ghostlike in the background, regal yet fading, while in the foreground a Satavahana die is about to stamp over his profile on a gleaming silver coin laid on an anvil.

dialogue.text: In the western Deccan, Nahapana’s face once shone on silver; then Gautamiputra Satakarni struck his mark upon it, and the fall of a Saka house was hammered into coin.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी दक्कन में कभी नाहपन का मुख चाँदी पर चमकता था; फिर गौतमीपुत्र सातकर्णि ने अपनी छाप जड़ी, और एक शक घराने का पतन सिक्कों पर ठुक गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on an open palm holding multiple bright silver coins, each bearing Nahapana’s bust and legends in Brahmi and Kharoshthi
panels.action: Nahapana, younger and confident, sits in a court at Nashik as a merchant kneels before him, presenting freshly minted silver coins stacked neatly in his open hands.

dialogue.text: Before the overstrikes, there was only Nahapana: Kshaharata ruler, Saka satrap, his name and titles running clean on silver across the western Deccan.

i18n.hi: ओवरस्ट्राइक से पहले बस नाहपन था: क्षहरात शासक, शक क्षत्रप, उसका नाम और उपाधियाँ साफ़–साफ़ चाँदी पर, पूरे पश्चिमी दक्कन में।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the western Deccan with stylised trade routes, caravans and ships moving toward a gleaming city
panels.action: Across a stylised map of the western Deccan, caravans wind along dusty roads and ships sail toward a harbour near the Western Ghats, where a city with warehouses and a mint rises.

dialogue.text: His coins moved with caravans and ships, from Nashik’s caves to the ports of the Konkan; silver tied Saka satraps to merchants, guilds and land.

i18n.hi: उसके सिक्के काफ़िलों और जहाज़ों के साथ चलते थे, नाशिक की गुफाओं से कोंकण के बंदरों तक; चाँदी ने शक क्षत्रपों को व्यापारियों, संघों और ज़मीन से कस कर बाँध रखा था।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a rock-cut cave, low-angle on Nahapana, with donors and monks around him
panels.action: Inside a half-finished rock-cut cave near Nashik, Nahapana stands in formal Saka attire beside a Buddhist monk, gesturing toward the pillars as stonecutters work in the background.

dialogue.text: In inscriptions near Nashik, the Kshaharata name stands firm; their satrap granted caves and land, their authority cut into stone as surely as into coin.

i18n.hi: नाशिक के पास के शिलालेखों में क्षहरात नाम अडिग खड़ा है; उनके क्षत्रप ने गुफाएँ और ज़मीन दान दी, उनकी सत्ता पत्थर पर भी उतनी ही गहरी कटी जितनी सिक्कों पर।

panels.shot: tight shot on Nahapana at a table of ledgers and coins, expression wary, shadow falling across his face
panels.action: Nahapana leans over a low wooden table scattered with ledgers and coin-piles, his brow furrowed, as a messenger from the east bows with a rolled letter in hand.

dialogue.text: But beyond his reach, Satavahana power stirred again; an old rival house, pushed back and divided, began to press once more from the eastern Deccan.

i18n.hi: पर उसकी पकड़ से बाहर, सातवाहन शक्ति फिर करवट ले रही थी; पुराना दुश्मन घराना, जो धकेला और बाँटा जा चुका था, फिर से पूर्वी दक्कन से धक्का देने लगा।

panels.shot: silhouetted long shot of two armies facing each other across a dusty plain, banners of different symbols fluttering
panels.action: On a hazy plain near the Western Ghats, two lines of troops stand in tense silence, Saka standards on one side and Satavahana emblems on the other, lances and horsemen outlined against the sky.

dialogue.text: The records do not name each battlefield, nor the exact year, but they remember a clash: Saka Kshaharatas against resurgent Satavahanas, contesting land, roads and the right to strike silver.

i18n.hi: लेख हर रणभूमि का नाम नहीं लेते, न ठीक साल बताते हैं, पर एक टक्कर याद रखते हैं: शक क्षहरात बनाम फिर से उभरे सातवाहन, ज़मीन, राहों और चाँदी गढ़ने के हक़ पर जंग।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nahapana on horseback in armour, looking back over his shoulder toward his men
panels.action: Nahapana rides along the front of his line, armour glinting, his mouth set in a hard line as he studies the Satavahana ranks in the distance while his officers watch him expectantly.

dialogue.speaker: nahapana_and_gautamiputra_satakarni
dialogue.text: Hold the roads, and the hills will follow.

i18n.hi: राहें थाम लो, पहाड़ अपने आप झुक जाएँगे।

panels.shot: abrupt cut to a quiet aftermath, wide shot of an abandoned satrapal camp with trampled standards and scattered coins
panels.action: The same field lies emptied of soldiers; Saka standards lie toppled in the dust, a few silver coins half-buried near abandoned carts, with vultures circling high above.

dialogue.text: The details of the defeat are lost, but the outcome is not: Kshaharata power broke, its lands and mints slipping into Satavahana hands.

i18n.hi: हार की बारीकियाँ गुम हैं, अंजाम नहीं: क्षहरात सत्ता टूट गई, उनकी ज़मीनें और टकसालें सातवाहनों के हाथ सरक गईं।

panels.shot: interior low-angle shot of a Satavahana mint, with workers, anvils and dies; focus on one worker placing a Nahapana coin on an anvil
panels.action: Inside a Satavahana mint, a worker places a worn Nahapana silver coin on an anvil while another holds a new die ready, stacks of similar coins in baskets around them.

dialogue.text: Then came the most silent battle: not on fields, but on anvils. Gautamiputra Satakarni took Nahapana’s own coins and overstruck them with his name.

i18n.hi: फिर आई सबसे खामोश जंग: न मैदानों पर, लोहार के सोंठों पर। गौतमीपुत्र सातकर्णि ने नाहपन के सिक्के उठाए और उन पर अपना नाम कूट दिया।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of hammer hitting the die, sparks and motion frozen, fragments of the old legend still visible beneath the new
panels.action: A hammer slams down on a die resting atop Nahapana’s coin; the moment is frozen, faint traces of the earlier bust and script visible beneath the newly forming Satavahana legend.

dialogue.text: Blow by blow, old legends were flattened; new letters, ‘Gautamiputra Satakarni’, pressed themselves over faint, stubborn traces of ‘Nahapana’.

i18n.hi: घाव पर घाव, पुरानी कथाएँ चपटी हो गईं; नए अक्षर ‘गौतमीपुत्र सातकर्णि’ ने ‘नाहपन’ की धुंधली, जिद्दी रेखाओं पर खुद को जमे–जोर से दबा दिया।

panels.shot: tabletop macro shot of several overstruck coins, one flipped to reveal ghostly under-type
panels.action: On a wooden table, a pile of freshly overstruck coins gleams; one coin is tilted so that Nahapana’s old profile shows faintly beneath Gautamiputra’s sharp new legends.

dialogue.text: Today, in the Jogalthambi hoard, Nahapana’s face still lurks under those overstrikes; a rare sight where two claims to power share the same thin disk of silver.

i18n.hi: आज भी जोगलथांबी के ख़ज़ाने में उन ओवरस्ट्राइक पर नाहपन का चेहरा दबा–दबा छिपा है; एक दुर्लभ नज़ारा, जहाँ दो सत्ता–दावे एक ही पतली चाँदी की टिकिया पर साथ बसते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Satavahana court, Gautamiputra’s mother seated as an inscription is being carved on a tablet
panels.action: In a Satavahana court setting, Gautami Balashri sits dignified as a scribe chisels words onto a stone slab, while attendants listen; a faint outline of cave architecture suggests Nashik.

dialogue.text: In the Nasik caves, Gautami Balashri’s inscription praised her son and declared that Gautamiputra had ‘uprooted the Kshaharatas’, claiming the satrapal house was finished.

i18n.hi: नासिक की गुफाओं में गौतमी बालश्री के शिलालेख ने बेटे की प्रशंसा की और घोषणा की कि गौतमीपुत्र ने ‘क्षहरातों को उखाड़ फेंका’, मानो क्षत्रपी घराना वहीं ख़त्म हो गया।

panels.shot: close-up of the stone inscription letters, hand and chisel in frame
panels.action: A mason’s hand holds a chisel to the stone, carving sharp Brahmi letters, chips of rock falling as the line about uprooting the Kshaharatas takes shape.

dialogue.text: The stone speaks with the victor’s voice; it does not doubt, it does not qualify. It simply states that the Kshaharata lineage was rooted out.

i18n.hi: पत्थर विजेता की ज़ुबान से बोलता है; न हिचकता है, न बहाना देता है। बस साफ़ कहता है कि क्षहरात वंश को जड़ से मिटा दिया गया।

panels.shot: documentary-style montage shot: scholars in a library, a hand turning a coin under a magnifying glass, another tracing an inscription rubbing
panels.action: In a modern study, a scholar examines an overstruck coin under a lens, another compares a rubbing of the Nashik inscription, shelves of books rising behind them in soft focus.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars match stone to silver; the inscription’s bold claim and the overstruck Jogalthambi coins together tell how a satrap’s fall was preserved in metal.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद विद्वान पत्थर को चाँदी से मिलाते हैं; शिलालेख का बुलंद दावा और ओवरस्ट्राइक जोगलथांबी के सिक्के मिलकर बताते हैं कि एक क्षत्रप का पतन धातु में कैसे बस गया।

panels.shot: thoughtful medium shot of a scholar gesturing at a timeline with uncertain ranges highlighted
panels.action: A historian stands before a board showing a timeline of the first and early second century, some stretches shaded to suggest uncertainty, as they point to a band labelled with both rulers’ names.

dialogue.text: Yet even now, the precise date of Nahapana’s defeat is debated; the coins and caves fix the sequence, but the exact year remains a gap between them.

i18n.hi: फिर भी आज तक नाहपन की हार की ठीक तारीख पर बहस है; सिक्के और गुफाएँ क्रम तो तय कर देते हैं, पर ठोस साल दोनों के बीच एक खाली जगह ही रह जाता है।

panels.shot: poised split-panel style shot: one side shows Nahapana regal, other shows a faint overstruck coin where he is barely visible
panels.action: On one side Nahapana stands tall in full regalia, on the other his figure dissolves into the faint under-image on a well-worn overstruck coin, the new legend more visible than his face.

dialogue.text: For Nahapana, the end of his line is not written in a single battle report; it is traced in ghosts of his portrait, shrinking beneath the sharper lines of another king’s name.

i18n.hi: नाहपन के लिए उसके घराने का अंत किसी एक युद्ध–वृत्तांत में नहीं लिखा; वह उसके चित्र की धुँधली परछाइयों में खिंचा है, जो धीरे–धीरे दूसरे राजा के तेज धार नाम के नीचे सिकुड़ती जाती हैं।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of a human hand holding an overstruck coin against the sky, light catching both layers
panels.action: A hand lifts an overstruck Nahapana coin toward the light of the sky; both the old and new designs glimmer faintly as if layered stories caught in metal.

dialogue.text: In that thin disk we see how power can be erased yet still endure as a shadow; the very coins once used to rule became the archive of a dynasty’s defeat.

i18n.hi: उस पतली टिकिया में दिखता है कैसे सत्ता मिट भी सकती है, फिर भी साए की तरह टिके रहती है; वही सिक्के जो कभी राज चलाने के लिए चले थे, एक वंश की हार का अभिलेख बन बैठे।

title_i18n.hi: जब गौतमीपुत्र ने सिक्कों पर वार किया

subtitle_i18n.en: How Silver Bore the Fall of the Kshaharatas
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे चाँदी ने क्षहरातों का पतन सहा
